identity.title: The ALMA-PILS survey: first detection of methyl isocyanide (CH<SUB>3</SUB>NC) in a solar-type protostar

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use ALMA observations from the Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey (PILS) to search for methyl isocyanide and compare its abundance with that of its isomer methyl cyanide.
The observations presented here were taken as part of the PILS program, an ALMA observing program to study IRAS 16293 in Band 7, between 329.147 GHz and 362.896 GHz.

claims.hypothesis: CH3NC is present in a solar-type protostar
claims.experiment: Search PILS Band 7 spectra at offset positions of IRAS 16293 A and B with new CDMS line list
claims.result: 16 lines detected in B above 3σ; none in A
claims.finding: First detection of CH3NC in a solar-type protostar

evidence.quote: This is the first detection of this molecule in a solar-type protostar. No lines are detected towards the offset position of IRAS 16293A.

claims.hypothesis: CH3NC abundance differs between A and B
claims.experiment: LTE fitting with CASSIS for B and 3σ upper limit for A
claims.result: CH3CN/CH3NC = 200 in B and >5517 in A
claims.finding: Significant chemical differentiation between A and B

evidence.quote: The lack of detection of methyl isocyanide in the second component in the IRAS 16293 binary, IRAS 16293A, shows that there is significant chemical differentiation between these sources.

claims.hypothesis: A chemical model with DeFrees isomerisation and H+CH3NC destruction reproduces observed ratios
claims.experiment: MAGICKAL models at two final densities
claims.result: High-density ratio ~2.5e6 consistent with A limit but not B; low-density ratio ~450 near B but density not representative
claims.finding: Model fails to match B at representative densities; consistent with A upper limits

evidence.quote: The chemical modelling is unable to match the observed CH$_3$CN/CH$_3$NC abundance ratio towards the B source at densities representative of that source. The modelling, however, is consistent with the upper limits for the A source.

claims.hypothesis: A gas-phase CH3NC destruction route not affecting CH3CN is needed
claims.result: Without gas-phase reaction ratio stays close to unity
claims.finding: Efficient gas-phase destruction of CH3NC is required

evidence.quote: This result shows that there needs to be some efficient mechanism for destruction of CH$_3$NC in the gas-phase that doesn’t operate on CH$_3$CN.

claims.hypothesis: Final collapse density controls the ratio
claims.experiment: Compare models at nH=1.6e7 and 6e10 cm^-3
claims.result: Ratios at 150 K differ by orders of magnitude
claims.finding: Ratio is very sensitive to final collapse density

evidence.quote: The chemical modelling has also shown that the CH$_3$CN/CH$_3$NC abundance ratio is very sensitive to the final collapse density.

limitations_admitted.value: H+CH3NC reaction and its barrier are speculative

evidence.quote: In particular, there is a large uncertainty on the barrier of the CH$_3$NC+H reaction as it likely does not equal the barrier on the HNC+H reaction.

evidence.quote: Also, although the low-density model fits the observations better than the high-density model, it may not be a representative density for the regions being probed by these observations.
